title: The Campaign
subtitle: Fifteen chapters of Napoleon's life, from a Corsican cadet to the legend of Saint Helena

chapters.title: The Cadet from Corsica
chapters.blurb: Napoleone di Buonaparte was born in Ajaccio on 15 August 1769, a year after France bought Corsica from Genoa. A royal scholarship sent the fierce little Corsican to military school at Brienne and then to the École Militaire in Paris, where he finished the two-year course in one. In September 1785, aged sixteen, he was commissioned a second lieutenant of artillery.

quote.text: I was born when my country was perishing.

chapters.title: The Siege of Toulon
chapters.blurb: The Revolution turned to Terror in 1793: the king was executed in January, and royalist Toulon surrendered its port and fleet to the British and Spanish. Captain Bonaparte, commanding the besiegers' artillery, saw that the heights over the harbor were the key. When they fell in December the enemy fleet sailed away, and the 24-year-old was promoted to brigadier general.

quote.text: The moral is to the physical as three to one.

chapters.title: A Whiff of Grapeshot
chapters.stage: General of the Army of the Interior, age 26
chapters.blurb: On 13 Vendémiaire (5 October 1795) royalist crowds rose against the Convention in Paris. Bonaparte, handed command at the last minute, had cannon brought up and cleared the streets with what Carlyle later called 'a whiff of grapeshot'. The grateful Directory gave him the Army of the Interior, then the Army of Italy, and in March 1796 he married Joséphine de Beauharnais.

quote.text: Death is nothing, but to live defeated and inglorious is to die daily.

chapters.title: The Italian Campaign
chapters.stage: Commander of the Army of Italy, age 26–28
chapters.blurb: In 1796 a ragged Army of Italy under its 26-year-old general beat the Piedmontese and Austrians in a string of battles: Montenotte, Lodi, Arcole, Rivoli. Mantua fell in early 1797 and Austria signed the Treaty of Campo Formio, ceding Belgium and conceding the left bank of the Rhine while France set up sister republics in northern Italy. Bonaparte returned to Paris a national hero.

quote.text: Soldiers, you are naked, ill fed… I will lead you into the most fertile plains in the world.
quote.by: Napoleon, proclamation to the Army of Italy, March 1796

chapters.title: The Egyptian Expedition
chapters.stage: Commander of the Army of the Orient, age 28–30
chapters.blurb: In May 1798 Bonaparte sailed for Egypt with some 35,000 troops and 160 scholars, seizing Malta on the way. He crushed the Mamluks at the Battle of the Pyramids, but Nelson destroyed his fleet at the Nile and a march into Syria broke on the walls of Acre. Leaving his army behind, he slipped back to France in October 1799, while the savants' work gave the world the Rosetta Stone and modern Egyptology.

quote.text: Soldiers, from the summit of these pyramids, forty centuries look down upon you.
quote.by: Napoleon, before the Battle of the Pyramids, 21 July 1798

chapters.title: The Coup of 18 Brumaire
chapters.blurb: France in late 1799 was bankrupt, riddled with corruption, and losing the war of the Second Coalition. On 18–19 Brumaire (9–10 November) Bonaparte, the abbé Sieyès, and Napoleon's brother Lucien overthrew the Directory at Saint-Cloud. The new Consulate had three consuls, but its First Consul held the real power: at thirty, Napoleon ruled France.

quote.text: Citizens, the Revolution is established upon the principles which began it: it is ended.

chapters.title: Marengo and the Consulate
chapters.place: The Great St Bernard Pass · Marengo · Paris
chapters.blurb: In May 1800 the First Consul led an army over the Great St Bernard Pass and beat the Austrians at Marengo on 14 June, a defeat turned into victory by Desaix's arrival. Peace followed: Lunéville with Austria (1801), the Concordat with the pope (1801), Amiens with Britain (1802). At home he founded the Bank of France, the lycées, and the Légion d'honneur, and in 1802 was made Consul for Life.

quote.text: It is with such baubles that men are led.
quote.by: Napoleon, defending the new Légion d'honneur, 1802

chapters.title: An Emperor Is Crowned
chapters.blurb: On 18 May 1804 the Senate proclaimed Napoleon Emperor of the French, and on 2 December, in Notre-Dame, he crowned himself with Pope Pius VII looking on. The same year saw the Civil Code, later called the Napoleonic Code, and the creation of eighteen Marshals of the Empire. The Republic's general had become a monarch with eagles, bees, and a court.

chapters.title: The Sun of Austerlitz
chapters.stage: Emperor of the French and King of Italy, age 36
chapters.blurb: When Britain, Austria, and Russia formed the Third Coalition in 1805, the Grande Armée marched from the Channel coast to the Danube in weeks, trapping an Austrian army at Ulm. Trafalgar (21 October) ended Napoleon's hopes at sea, but on 2 December, the coronation's anniversary, he destroyed the Russo-Austrian army at Austerlitz. The Treaty of Pressburg stripped Austria of Venetia and made Bavaria and Württemberg kingdoms.

chapters.title: From Jena to Tilsit
chapters.place: Jena · Eylau · Friedland · the raft on the Niemen
chapters.blurb: In 1806 Napoleon dissolved the thousand-year-old Holy Roman Empire, gathered the German states into a Confederation of the Rhine, and put brothers on the thrones of Naples and Holland. Prussia's army was wrecked at Jena and Auerstedt in a single day (14 October 1806). After the bloody draw at Eylau and the victory at Friedland, Napoleon and Tsar Alexander I met on a raft on the Niemen and divided Europe at Tilsit.

chapters.title: The Zenith of Empire
chapters.blurb: By 1810–11 the Empire was at its height: 130 départements from Hamburg to Rome, a ring of kingdoms ruled by Bonapartes and marshals, and an Austrian archduchess, Marie-Louise, as empress. But the Spanish 'ulcer' opened in 1808 bled the army in guerrilla war, Wagram (1809) was won at a heavy price, and the Continental System was straining every ally.

chapters.stage: Commander of the Grande Armée, age 43
chapters.place: The Niemen · Borodino · Moscow · the Berezina
chapters.blurb: In June 1812 the Grande Armée, more than 600,000 men and barely half of them French, crossed the Niemen into Russia. Borodino (7 September) was the bloodiest day of the wars; Moscow was entered a week later and burned. Alexander refused to negotiate, and the retreat through snow and Cossacks destroyed the army. Napoleon raced back to Paris in December.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Nations

chapters.place: Longwood House, Saint Helena · Les Invalides
chapters.blurb: Exiled to Saint Helena, 1,200 miles off the coast of Africa, Napoleon spent five and a half years at damp Longwood House dictating his memoirs and feuding with Governor Hudson Lowe. He died on 5 May 1821. In 1840 his body was returned to Paris in triumph and laid under the dome of Les Invalides; his nephew became Napoleon III in 1852, and his Code, his legend, and his wars still shape Europe.
